subject: drow poisoning timeline
fact: The poison was transferred via a book licked by the killer, and the act occurred during a day of drugging and emotional distress.
source_quote: I was drugged. I was upset. I don't know what I was thinking.

subject: eight o'clock meeting
fact: Kalan met with Janussi at eight o'clock to request additional watchers, and was refused; this refusal may have triggered the murder, as Janussi was aware of security vulnerabilities; the timing suggests the killer acted within hours of this confrontation.
source_quote: The eight o'clock meeting where he'd pressed Janussi for more watchers and been refused.

subject: eight o'clock meeting with Janussi
fact: Kalan met with Janussi at eight o’clock to request more watchers and was refused — a key event in his timeline before the murder.
source_quote: The eight o'clock meeting where he'd pressed Janussi for more watchers and been refused.

subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between two events in the session.
source_quote: An hour later

subject: midnight curfew
fact: Daral will be kept under watch until midnight, when a cleric and sword capable of drawing poison are within arm's reach.
source_quote: We'd keep Daral close until midnight — a cleric who could draw poison out, and a sword that could do the same, both within arm's reach.

subject: midnight deadline
fact: Daral Yashenti is to be held under surveillance until midnight, when a cleric and a sword capable of drawing poison will be brought to his side. If he dies after that hour, it will be interpreted as evidence that he was the poisoner — the poison was meant to kill only if he were innocent. The timing is a ritualistic test of guilt.
source_quote: We'd keep Daral close until midnight.

subject: morning of the murder
fact: On the morning of the murder, Kalan conducted an inspection just after eight, established a cordon, posted a watcher, and doubled the guard at the High Tower Library — all documented to establish his whereabouts.
source_quote: The morning of the murder: the inspection just after eight, the cordon, the posted watcher...

subject: night of the murder
fact: The murder occurred on the night of the incident, with Janussi consuming the poison during the day and dying at midnight; Kalan’s timeline places him at the Chamber of Lost Lore, visiting Sylvira Savikas at quarter-past-ten, and inspecting the High Tower before the murder; the impersonation of Sylvira Savikas occurred during this window.
source_quote: The quarter-past-ten visit to Sylvira Savikas over some cosmological question.

subject: quarter-past-ten visit to Sylvira Savikas
fact: Kalan visited Sylvira Savikas at 10:15 for a cosmological question — later revealed to have been an impersonator, undermining his alibi and timeline.
source_quote: The quarter-past-ten visit to Sylvira Savikas over some cosmological question.

subject: session date
fact: The events described occur during the investigation phase of Chapter 54, following the Candlekeep Murders. No specific calendar date is given, but the narrative implies immediate post-crime activity, with the body being removed and the investigation initiated without delay.
source_quote: We came into the chapter house to find her already in conference with someone new...

subject: session date
fact: The events occur in the context of a murder investigation at Candlekeep, with no explicit in-world calendar date provided.

subject: Session Date
fact: The events of Glabbagool’s trial and transformation occurred during a session in which Zalthir acknowledges he has missed many lessons and spent many days sleeping.
source_quote: There are, by now, a great many days I was sleeping. Was I ever there?

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 11th day of the month, during the interrogation of Daral Yashenti at the Hearth.
source_quote: The eleven o'clock meeting came out without resistance

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493 DR.
source_quote: On the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493

subject: Time before 9 a.m.
fact: The critical temporal anchor for Bookwyrm’s alibi is the period before 9 a.m. — the window during which the murder may have occurred or been concealed, and when the impersonator was active.
source_quote: I also want to understand where Bookwyrm was before nine in the morning…

subject: Timeline of the murder
fact: The murder occurred sometime before nine in the morning; Bookwyrm’s whereabouts during that time are unaccounted for, and Fheminor Scrivenbark was beaten before death — possibly at eight — suggesting a sequence of events leading to the killing.
source_quote: I also want to understand where Bookwyrm was before nine in the morning.

subject: assault on Janussi
fact: Daral may have caught Janussi lightly on the nose during a physical altercation.
source_quote: Daral may have caught him lightly on the nose

subject: bonding of Zalthir and Glabbagool
fact: Zalthir and Glabbagool formed a permanent, symbiotic bond within the Whispering Dome. Glabbagool chose Zalthir not by force but by silent alignment, settling on his arm like a natural extension. The bond grants Glabbagool mobility and Zalthir enhanced combat abilities, including teleportation, acidic strikes, and dissolution via corrosive embrace. The event marks Zalthir’s transformation from a negligent student to a vessel of unlearned wisdom.
source_quote: Glabbagool and Zalthir, together now.

subject: book page flicking
fact: Daral flicked through the pages of the poisoned book with his finger, indicating direct contact with the poison.
source_quote: he wet his finger and began flicking through the pages

subject: book seizure
fact: The book was seized as evidence after Thorin revealed the poisoning method, and Daral was held under guard until midnight with a cleric and sword ready to extract poison, in case he was the victim.
source_quote: We took it. We'd keep Daral close until midnight — a cleric who could draw poison out, and a sword that could do the same, both within arm's reach.

subject: collaboration proposal
fact: Zalthir and Kalan propose a collaborative investigation — offline, private work streams, and a synchronized review of all evidence — to overcome mutual distrust and uncover the truth.
source_quote: I hope you actually used the word sync up...

subject: collaboration proposal between Thorin and Kalan
fact: Thorin proposed an offline sync-up of investigative streams with Kalan, Grygum, Zalthir, and Daz, resulting in Kalan agreeing to a private, five-stream merge of findings.
source_quote: He proposed it in the most extraordinary terms — offline chat, private work streams, a meeting to examine everything one by one, the four of us and him, five streams, merge it all in a few hours. ... 'I hope you actually used the word sync up,' I said. 'That makes me happy.'

subject: Corpse Silence Claim
fact: Kalan Strongbranch claimed the corpse was silenced by an imposter, preventing it from answering questions — this assertion is hearsay, unverifiable, and potentially a cover for his own involvement.
source_quote: Kalan said they'd put the question to the corpse, and that it didn't work. And that didn't work because of Y.

subject: Corrosive Embrace Demonstration
fact: Glabbagool demonstrated his corrosive embrace on a restrained target, revealing it causes dissolution — not a wound — leaving nothing remaining after the target is bound.
source_quote: It was not a wound. It was dissolution. A target restrained, nothing left to hold by the end of it.

subject: Daral's defense of the book
fact: Daral's defense of the book is referenced by Zalthir as the moment he delivered a small theology lecture about whether books are for enjoyment or knowledge, which Thorin patiently dismantled, and after which Daral took the book back and claimed Janussi had sat upon him like a common thug.
source_quote: Daral's defense was a small theology lecture about whether books are for enjoyment or knowledge, which Thorin patiently dismantled, and at the end of it Daral had taken his book back, Janussi had *sat upon him like a common thug*, and in self-defense Daral *may have caught him lightly on the nose*.

subject: Discovery of Fabricated Notes
fact: The investigators discovered that their own notes had been altered — the entry for Fheminor Scrivenbark was erased — indicating internal sabotage or magical tampering within Candlekeep’s records.
source_quote: Our own notes had started lying to us.

subject: duration of investigation constraint
fact: The investigators are told they will only get to chase a handful of threads before the investigation moves on without them.
source_quote: the constraint landed — that we'd only get to chase a handful of threads before the thing moved on without us

subject: Erasure of Fheminor Scrivenbark’s name from notes
fact: The team’s own investigation notes have been altered, removing Fheminor Scrivenbark’s name from an entry that otherwise reflects aligned priorities — suggesting internal sabotage or memory manipulation.
source_quote: Our own notes had started lying to us.

subject: false identity
fact: Someone impersonated Sylvira Savikas the night of the murder.
source_quote: Is he aware that someone was pretending to be Sylvira Savikas the night of the murder?

subject: false Sylvira Savikas impersonation
fact: Someone impersonated Sylvira Savikas the night of the murder, a fact unknown to Kalan until revealed by Thorin, causing him to acknowledge new information and reconsider his assumptions.
source_quote: Is he aware that someone was pretending to be Sylvira Savikas the night of the murder?" ... He went still. "No. That is new information." ... "You are very good at this.

subject: glabbagool bonding
fact: Glabbagool bonded with Zalthir by settling along his forearm, appearing as part of his scales.
source_quote: Glabbagool flowed up onto my arm... settling along my forearm like he had measured it in advance

subject: Glabbagool's stillness
fact: Glabbagool's stillness is referenced by Zalthir as the moment he held perfect silence for the better part of a minute in response to the monk’s question about the art of movement, a feat Zalthir recognized as superior to his own failed attempts at the same discipline.
source_quote: Glabbagool went still. Not paused. Still. The difference matters. Paused costs something; still costs nothing. The better part of a minute passed.

subject: Glabbagool's Transformation
fact: Glabbagool underwent a transformation during the trial at the Whispering Dome, achieving perfect stillness, answering the monk’s question with wisdom, and bonding to Zalthir with new abilities and physical manifestations.
source_quote: Glabbagool went still. Not paused. Still. The difference matters. Paused costs something; still costs nothing.

subject: Glabbagool's transformation
fact: Glabbagool's transformation is referenced by Zalthir as the moment he flowed onto Zalthir’s arm, claimed "We ride," and acquired four eyes that blinked from Zalthir’s scales, while also retaining the ability to teleport in darkness, throw a flurry of strikes, and deliver a corrosive embrace.
source_quote: And he flowed up onto my arm. *Glabbagool and Zalthir, together now,* he said, settling along my forearm like he had measured it in advance. ... Four, as it turned out, blinking up from my own scales.

subject: High Tower key transfer
fact: Kalan transferred the second High Tower key to an unknown individual shortly before vanishing; he insists the key is no longer in his possession and that its location must remain secret; the key is believed to be retrievable via a summoning spell tied to a sapphire, allowing it to be hidden anywhere and recalled on demand.
source_quote: I have given it now to someone who is not me.

subject: impersonation of Sylvira Savikas
fact: Someone impersonated Sylvira Savikas on the night of the murder, a fact unknown to Kalan until revealed by Zalthir, which undermines his entire theory of the crime.
source_quote: Is he aware that someone was pretending to be Sylvira Savikas the night of the murder?

subject: Impersonation of Sylvira Savikas at night
fact: An individual wearing Sylvira Savikas’s face was seen walking the halls with a lantern in the dead of night, indicating a deliberate act of deception to confuse the investigation or gain access to restricted areas.
source_quote: Sylvira — or somebody wearing her face — had been walking the halls in the dead of night with a lantern.

subject: investigator collaboration
fact: Kalan proposed a private sync-up meeting with five streams to merge findings and resolve contradictions.
source_quote: A meeting to examine everything one by one, the four of us and him, five streams, merge it all in a few hours.

subject: Janussi's murder
fact: Janussi was killed by ingestion of 'midnight tears,' a Feywild poison that activates at midnight; the poison was administered via a book he licked his fingers to turn, leaving blackened lips and fingers; his heart was removed post-mortem to prevent resurrection; the key to the High Tower was hidden in a locket around his neck, which was stolen; two individuals searched the apartment — one who knew the key’s location, one who did not and rifled the safe.
source_quote: The heart was gone. Two people had stood over him — one who knew exactly where the locket-key hid, and one who didn't and tore through the safe instead.

subject: Kalan’s removal from the case
fact: Kalan was officially removed from the investigation by Bookwyrm, which he believes was done to protect someone — but Zalthir suggests it may have been to ensure the case was bungled.
source_quote: He staged it — reminded us, twice, that he had been wanted off the case.

subject: Kalan's timeline reconstruction
fact: Kalan provided a detailed timeline of his movements on the day of the murder, including his refusal of additional watchers at eight, his visit to Sylvira Savikas, and his return to the Chamber of Lost Lore for research.
source_quote: the eight o'clock meeting where he'd pressed Janussi for more watchers and been refused, the quarter-past-ten visit to Sylvira Savikas over some cosmological question, the return to the Chamber of Lost Lore for private research.

subject: key transfer
fact: Kalan transferred the second High Tower key to someone who is not himself, and now holds no key.
source_quote: I have given it now to someone who is not me.

subject: key transfer from Kalan to Grygum
fact: Kalan Strongbranch transferred the second High Tower key to Grygum during a private meeting, after declaring he no longer held it and that entry to the tower is always observed.
source_quote: Kalan stepped out of a doorway we hadn't clocked, swept the corridor left, then right, and pressed a small brass key specifically into the cleric's palm. ... I have given it now to someone who is not me.

subject: Key Transfer to Grygum
fact: Kalan Strongbranch covertly transferred the second High Tower key to Grygum in a hidden corridor, bypassing all other investigators; this act suggests he distrusts the group and anticipates his own death.
source_quote: Kalan stepped out of a doorway we hadn't clocked... pressed a small brass key specifically into the cleric's palm.

subject: murder at the High Tower Library
fact: A murder occurred at the High Tower Library, with signs of magical interference, a missing key hidden in a locket, and evidence suggesting the killer was a magic user who bypassed arcane and mundane locks.
source_quote: He noticed the murderer was a magic user who could circumvent arcane and mundane locks.

subject: murderer's method
fact: The murderer is a magic user who can circumvent arcane and mundane locks with talking magic.
source_quote: Magic that could talk any lock open, arcane or iron, the very highest order of that art.

subject: murder of Janussi
fact: Janussi was murdered by ingestion of midnight tears administered via a poisoned book, with his heart removed post-mortem to prevent resurrection, and the High Tower key stolen from his locket.
source_quote: He died at roughly midnight. ... The heart hacked out — after death, to spoil resurrection. ... The key was in the locket. The locket was around the keeper's neck. The locket was gone.

subject: Murder of Janussi
fact: Janussi, a high-ranking scholar, was murdered by poison; his body was found in a sealed chamber, his mouth locked as if by supernatural means, and his tower key is missing; the murder triggered a power vacuum and an official investigation.
source_quote: The whole pack of them, shouting over a body.

subject: Murder of Janussi
fact: The murder of Janussi triggered the current investigation, destabilizing the scholarly hierarchy and prompting conflicting agendas among council members; it is the central event around which all suspicions orbit.
source_quote: The whole pack of them, shouting over a body.

subject: murder timing
fact: The victim died at midnight after ingesting midnight tears poison, likely via licking a poisoned page.
source_quote: He died at roughly midnight. His fingers were black, his lips were black.

subject: poison delivery method
fact: Midnight tears poison is ingested and activates at midnight, with color change upon contact with saliva.
source_quote: The dust stays pale ochre. What darkens it is saliva.

subject: poison delivery method
fact: The poison was delivered not through ingestion or injection, but via contamination of a book’s pages, activated by the victim’s habitual act of licking his fingers while reading.
source_quote: Some liquid had gotten onto his finger, and the finger had gone black... The dust stays pale ochre. What darkens it is saliva.

subject: poison discovery in Flora Theca
fact: Grygum discovered the properties of midnight tears in Archibald Roots, Jr.'s book *Fey-mous Flowers & Fungi*, confirming its Feywild origin, delayed lethality until midnight, and activation via saliva.
source_quote: I opened it. ... Midnight tears. A highly toxic pale ochre dust, made from the pollen of a plant usually found only in the Feywild. ... The creature that ingests this poison suffers no effect until the stroke of midnight. ... What darkens it is saliva.

subject: poisoning of Janussi
fact: Janussi was poisoned via a book that had been licked by Daral Yashenti, whose finger carried the toxin from repeated page-turning. The poison was not administered by violence but by subtle, ritualistic contact — a method that implicates the victim’s own engagement with the object of affection and anger. The act was deliberate, concealed, and tied to emotional conflict.
source_quote: The book had been in his collection for years... he wet his finger and began flicking through the pages.

subject: sequence of council meeting
fact: The Council of the Great Readers dispersed before the investigators arrived, and the body was taken to the Shrine of Oghma after the meeting.
source_quote: The Council of the Great Readers had dispersed. We came into the chapter house to find her already in conference with someone new... The body went to be purified.

subject: sequence of investigation steps
fact: The group decides to start together and split later when two doors open at once.
source_quote: we'd start together and peel off when two doors opened at once

subject: sequence of suspect elimination
fact: Daral and Sylvira are crossed off as suspects based on gut feeling, not evidence.
source_quote: Daral, we crossed off — not by evidence, by gut... Sylvira, same logic, different reason

subject: sequence of witness interviews
fact: Daz is assigned to interview Fheminor Scrivenbark first, as he has the least amount of time or talk.
source_quote: Daz took Fheminor. 'I'm looking at the ones that have the least amount of time, or probably have the least amount to talk about'

subject: silent communication lesson
fact: Zalthir missed the lesson on silent communication, while Glabbagool mastered it by going still.
source_quote: If I had paid more attention to the classes on silent communication, I would know exactly what Glabbagool's answer meant... He had mastered the one lesson I most thoroughly missed, and he had done it in under a minute, by going still.

subject: silent communication mastery
fact: Glabbagool mastered silent communication by going still, while Zalthir had missed the lesson.
source_quote: He had mastered the one lesson I most thoroughly missed, and he had done it in under a minute, by going still.

subject: summoning spell revelation
fact: Grygum identified the sapphire summoning spell as a method to recall a hidden object to the caster’s hand, clarifying that it does not work on worn items and thus enables the key to be hidden in plain sight by being stored elsewhere.
source_quote: It's an old summoning working — the kind that calls a single hidden thing back into your hand. ... It doesn't work if— although you'd find out who was holding it. ... You can put it someplace, you can throw it into a river or whatever. Nobody will find it, and then when you need it back, boom.

subject: the poisoning of Janussi
fact: The poisoning of Janussi is referenced by Zalthir as the event in which poison was carried on a book and transferred by a man licking his finger and turning the pages, leading to Daral Yashenti’s interrogation and the eventual seizure of the book as evidence.
source_quote: Janussi had been poisoned, the poison carried on a book, transferred by a man licking his finger and turning the pages.

subject: time of Fheminor's beating
fact: Fheminor Scrivenbark was beaten up at eight in the morning, which is a key timing detail.
source_quote: find out when the man got beaten up, because beat-up-at-eight tells a different story

subject: travel to Sloobludop
fact: Sloobludop is approximately eight days away via the Darklake.
source_quote: the town of Sloopdopblop is just eight days away

subject: victim's death
fact: The victim died at precisely midnight after ingesting midnight tears — a Feywild poison that becomes lethal only when mixed with the sap of a specific Feywild tree, and activated by saliva from finger-licking while reading.
source_quote: You consume it, you're fine — apparently fine — and then you're dead at midnight.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is a high-ranking authority who has officially barred Kalan from the investigation; her motives are unclear, but Kalan suspects she is either protecting the murderer or has been manipulated into sidelining him; Zalthir and Thorin consider her role central to the conspiracy, possibly as a puppet or a participant.
source_quote: Bookwyrm had made it official that he was to be nowhere near it.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is an authority figure who officially removed Kalan from the case, possibly to protect someone involved in the murder or to obstruct the investigation, and is suspected of being complicit or manipulated.
source_quote: Bookwyrm had made it official that he was to be nowhere near it.

subject: Council of the Great Readers
fact: The Council of the Great Readers has dispersed following the murders; members including A'lai Aivenmore, Kazryn Nyantani, and Alkrist are vying for control, demanding leadership changes and accountability, but none have been formally appointed.
source_quote: A'lai Aivenmore wanting a vote and new leadership... Kazryn Nyantani... cutting through with first you must find the murderer.

subject: Council of the Great Readers
fact: The Council of the Great Readers has dispersed, indicating a prior governing body that no longer holds active authority over the investigation. Their absence leaves Bookwyrm as the de facto authority in Candlekeep’s current crisis.
source_quote: The Council of the Great Readers had dispersed.

subject: High Tower
fact: The High Tower uses a summoning spell requiring a sapphire to recall hidden objects, potentially revolutionizing how its keys are secured — not carried, but summoned when needed.
source_quote: You don't hide the key on a body where someone can search it. You hide it nowhere at all, and you summon it when the door is in front of you.

subject: Shadow Monks
fact: The Shadow Monks are a monastic order that teaches silent communication, stillness, and the art of movement, with rituals involving shuttered rooms, incense, ink-stained hands, and controlled breathing.
source_quote: Silent discussion. Communication without sound. I remember the light through the shutters. I do not remember the lesson.

subject: The Great Readers
fact: The Great Readers are a powerful, secretive group within the magical hierarchy; Kalan suspects one of them is the murderer and believes Bookwyrm may be protecting them or has been coerced into removing him from the case; their influence extends to manipulating investigations and eliminating inconvenient investigators.
source_quote: I believe you're only being employed so you're likely to bungle the case, or else be silent if you do happen upon the right scent.

subject: The Great Readers
fact: The Great Readers are an influential organization suspected by Kalan of being involved in the murder, with possible ties to Bookwyrm’s decision to fire Kalan in order to protect one of their own.
source_quote: What he suspected, he said, was that one of the Great Readers was the murderer...

subject: The Keepers of the Tomes
fact: The Keepers of the Tomes are an institutional hierarchy that values scholarly integrity and forbids the sale of sacred texts. Violations — such as attempting to sell poetry for demonic treatises — are met with severe punishment, but Daral’s case suggests inconsistency or leniency in enforcement. The position of keeper is highly contested, with multiple aspirants vying for power.
source_quote: An uneducated bookseller is what he is." "May the gods bless whoever bumped him off.

subject: The Scholarly Council of the Deneir's Sanctum
fact: The Scholarly Council is fractured, with members vying for control after a murder; A'lai Aivenmore seeks new leadership, Fheminor Scrivenbark questions Janussi’s successor, Kazryn Nyantani demands the murderer be found, and Alkrist demands the gate warden be dismissed.
source_quote: A'lai Aivenmore wanting a vote and new leadership. The dowdy halfling, Fheminor Scrivenbark, asking whether Janussi had named a successor. Kazryn Nyantani... cutting through with first you must find the murderer. Alkrist... the gate warden needs to be dismissed.

subject: The Watchers of the High Tower
fact: An unseen organization or force permanently surveils the High Tower, rendering unauthorized entry detectable regardless of key possession — their identity and allegiance are unknown.
source_quote: The tower is watched. Always. People stand at it whether the key is in someone's pocket or not.

subject: The Whispering Dome
fact: The Whispering Dome is a sacred space where supplicants undergo silent, introspective trials to gain self-knowledge. It values stillness, non-verbal understanding, and philosophical insight. The monks there recognize wisdom in silence and punish ignorance of its lessons — as Zalthir’s absence during the silent communication class demonstrates.
source_quote: What is the art of movement.

subject: bag of holding
fact: The bag of holding contains drow that require monitoring, per Glabbagool's instruction.
source_quote: the drow in the bag of holding still needed watching

subject: bag of holding
fact: The bag of holding is referenced by Glabbagool as containing drow who still need watching, and whose presence he reminds Zalthir of even during his own transformation.
source_quote: Before he settled in, he reminded me the drow in the bag of holding still needed watching.

subject: blingdenstone
fact: Blingdenstone is a location Glabbagool survived during his history.
source_quote: He had survived Blingdenstone and the ooze crisis

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a place where deception is reflexive among scholars, and physical evidence is considered more reliable than testimony.
source_quote: Down here everyone lies as a reflex. You can't out-talk a culture that talks for a living. But a smear of poison on a dead man's fingers doesn't have a motive.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a place where investigations are artificially constrained by external deadlines, with the threat of further murders looming.
source_quote: Apparently things keep happening while you're standing around thinking. Grygum put it plainest: "There'll be more murders."

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a vast, labyrinthine library where investigators are warned they may easily become lost, and where all movement requires an escort.
source_quote: The library is very easy to get lost in.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a vast, labyrinthine library-fortress where scholars live and work; its complexity makes navigation difficult without guides, and its culture of secrecy, deception, and intellectual rivalry enables crimes to be concealed.
source_quote: The library is very easy to get lost in.

subject: Candlekeep Chapter House
fact: The chapter house is the central location of the investigation, where Bookwyrm met with Kei Tigersteel and later convened with the investigators. It contains Deneir's Sanctum, now repurposed as the investigators’ office, and is described as easy to get lost in, requiring escorts to navigate.
source_quote: We came into the chapter house to find her already in conference with someone new...

subject: Candlekeep library layout
fact: Candlekeep is described as very easy to get lost in.
source_quote: The library is very easy to get lost in.

subject: Chamber of Lost Lore
fact: The Chamber of Lost Lore is where Kalan conducted private research after his visit to Sylvira Savikas, possibly seeking information relevant to the case.
source_quote: The return to the Chamber of Lost Lore for private research.

subject: Chamber of Lost Lore
fact: The Chamber of Lost Lore is where Kalan conducted private research and where the murder investigation’s timeline places his morning inspection and the posting of emergency guards.
source_quote: the return to the Chamber of Lost Lore for private research. ... the morning of the murder: the inspection just after eight, the cordon, the posted watcher, the state of emergency, the doubled guard at the High Tower Library.

subject: chapter house
fact: The chapter house is where Bookwyrm was found in conference with Kei Tigersteel, a slender half-elf with a precise goatee, and where the Council of the Great Readers had dispersed.
source_quote: We came into the chapter house to find her already in conference with someone new — a slender half-elf, perhaps fifty, bald scalp framed by black side whiskers chiseled down into a precise goatee.

subject: Council of the Great Readers
fact: The Council of the Great Readers is a disbanded governing body of Candlekeep, whose members convened after the murder to debate leadership and procedure.
source_quote: The Council of the Great Readers had dispersed.

subject: Deneir's Sanctum
fact: Deneir's Sanctum is a shrine and library dedicated to the art of writing, now assigned as the investigators’ private office. It is guarded by Vooshadi Moonriver, and its offering as a workspace is viewed with suspicion due to the controlled access and implied surveillance.
source_quote: Then she took us to a nearby room, Deneir's Sanctum... and offered it up as our office.

subject: Deneir's Sanctum
fact: Deneir's Sanctum is a shrine and library dedicated to the art of writing, offered by Bookwyrm as the investigators' office, with Fembris Lancer assigned to fetch witnesses and Vooshadi Moonriver to guard the door.
source_quote: Then she took us to a nearby room, Deneir's Sanctum, a little shrine and library given over to the art of writing, and offered it up as our office. Fembris would fetch any witness we named. Vooshadi Moonriver would stand the door — "we wouldn't want anyone the investigators don't want to come in, to come in."

subject: Deneir's Sanctum
fact: Deneir's Sanctum is a shrine and library dedicated to the art of writing, offered by Bookwyrm as the investigators' office; its apparent generosity is suspected to mask surveillance, as the room’s privacy cannot be confirmed and tools for reading through walls fail inside it.
source_quote: It's nice and all to offer up that we can use the office... but it's also a little suspect.

subject: Deneir's Sanctum
fact: Deneir's Sanctum is offered as the investigators' office, a shrine and library dedicated to the art of writing.
source_quote: Deneir's Sanctum, a little shrine and library given over to the art of writing

subject: Deneir's Sanctum
fact: Deneir's Sanctum is suspected by the investigators to be surveilled, as the generosity of its offer is interpreted as potentially manipulative.
source_quote: It doesn't seem just friendly... It's nice and all to offer up that we can use the office, and that they'll go fetch people, and all of those sorts of things, but it's also a little suspect.

subject: Deneir's Sanctum
fact: Deneir's Sanctum is the central investigation hub, presented as a safe space for interviews, but its perceived openness raises suspicion of surveillance or manipulation; Bookwyrm’s gesture of trust feels performative.
source_quote: Deneir's Sanctum felt like a gift.

subject: Flora Theca
fact: The Flora Theca is a research chamber with towering shelves, used by Grygum to uncover the truth behind the murder through botanical and magical texts, and is the site of the critical deduction that the book itself was the weapon.
source_quote: Just stacks, and quiet, and the work. I started pulling tomes.

subject: Flora Theca

subject: Bookwyrm

subject: Bookwyrm

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes fictional detectives have perfect memories.
source_quote: "I don't know if they do," Thorin said. "I think real detectives just write everything down." "Poirot never does." "No, he doesn't. It's like, at the end of the episode, he's like, okay, everybody sit down, I'm gonna tell you what's what." There was a warmth in it I rarely heard from him. "My wife and I have watched the entire series, and we're down to the last episode, and we're saving it. I'm not sure for why, but —" I let them have it. I was running a different question, the one Thorin eventually asked aloud as we walked. "Who are we working for, exactly?" "Justice," said Grygum. The first rule of any House: know who holds the debt before you decide whether to collect it. Thorin, in his blunt giant-raised way, got to the same place from the other direction. "I guess, who has the power to fire us and tell us to go away?" Bookwyrm. Of course Bookwyrm. We were working for Bookwyrm, and Thorin — who hates the whole rotten apparatus of who-knows-what — put the obvious crack in it before I had to. "I'm just saying, like, if Bookwyrm ended up doing it, which I don't think she did, but… then." A beat. "This could get awkward." It could. I sorted her into the column marked *not above suspicion* and kept walking. The Council of the Great Readers had dispersed. We came into the chapter house to find her already in conference with someone new — a slender half-elf, perhaps fifty, bald scalp framed by black side whiskers chiseled down into a precise goatee. I would have liked to know what they were saying before the door opened. So would everyone. We tried; the trouble is that I had the right tools for reading a page — through a closed door, those tools were the wrong shape entirely. Whatever passed between them, it stayed between them. The moon elf scribes moved to halt us at the threshold. Bookwyrm waved them off and ushered us in herself, all warmth, and introduced the man as Kei Tigersteel — Lorekeeper of Candlekeep, priest of the Temple of Oghma, "the library's spiritual leader." I noted the seating and the easy way she dismissed him a moment later: *yes, Kei, you can take the body to the Shrine of Oghma for purification.* The body went to be purified. Now she was alone with us, which I also noted. "Have you concluded your investigation of the crime scene?" Very serious now. We had. Grygum confirmed it plainly. Thorin pressed her to keep the room sealed, and she agreed three times over — *of course, of course, of course* — which is two more agreements than a thing requires. Then she took us to a nearby room, Deneir's Sanctum, a little shrine and library given over to the art of writing, and offered it up as our office. Fembris would fetch any witness we named. Vooshadi Moonriver would stand the door — *we wouldn't want anyone the investigators don't want to come in, to come in.* And one more thing, lightly placed: we shouldn't move through Candlekeep without one of them. The library is very easy to get lost in. I have an alternative reading of generosity, which is that it is rarely free. "Do we think the room is, like, bugged," I asked the others once we had a moment, "or has, like, secret — like, the stuff we do in there is actually going to be private to us, or do we need —" I kept going, because the offer was too clean. "It's nice and all to offer up that we can use the office, and that they'll go fetch people, and all of those sorts of things, but it's also a little suspect. Like, maybe they're involved, and somehow…" "It doesn't seem just friendly," Grygum said. I asked him to say it again. "It doesn't seem just friendly." "It could be just friendly." I meant it as a hypothesis to be tested, not a comfort. "I mean, it could be that they genuinely want to get to the bottom of this." "Yeah," I said. "It could be." Both columns stayed open. She wanted to know what we'd told her. So did I — it pays to know exactly how much of an account you've already handed over. "Generalities," I said. "That we went and talked to all the people that we could talk to. And we're forming an opinion on what may have happened, and who — like, we have a couple suspects that we would like to pursue, due to perceiving that they may have a motivation, or that other people have pointed them out. We're still —" "Is there any — any suspects in particular?" The question came a half-step too fast. "We refuse to comment on ongoing," Thorin said. "Yeah," I added, "it's an ongoing investigation, and it's not, not proper for us to share that at this time." "Very well," she said. And then she sat there, and she did the thing I'd been waiting for. "Was there nobody that you wished to start your investigation with?" That is not an idle question. That is a question that wants a name back so it can measure where we're pointed. Thorin deflected — *not quite sure who we're gonna talk to next, but you shouldn't read into that* — and I gave her one harmless witness to chew on, Ms. Hollypocket, whom we'd already seen anyway. A name that costs nothing tells you what the asker does with a name. What she did was want Sylvira Savikas. She never said it. She didn't have to; the want came off her like heat off the smelters. Someone had impersonated Sylvira — Grygum thought it made perfect sense, and tactically it did, the impersonated woman might know who would wear her face. It also meant the most powerful person in this building had a strong, unstated preference about where we aimed first. I sorted it: *Bookwyrm steers toward Sylvira.* I had no idea yet whether that was the helpful instinct of someone who wants the thing solved, or a thumb on the scale of an investigation she'd rather not have tilted toward herself. I left that account open too. Then the practical question — together or apart. Thorin liked us as a wall. "It's more imposing to have all, like, you know, four, five, seven, eight, ten of us show up in a room." Grygum wanted to start together and branch later. The reasoning was simple enough: split, and we cover the poison and Sylvira at once, but each of us walks into his own conversation alone, no second pair of hands to steady the work. "Since we're separated, whatever each of us draws, that's what we're stuck with," Thorin said. That was the trade. More ground, less margin. I could live with that. --- ## Thorin — Investigation Strategy and Suspect Review I have spent enough time in the Underdark to know what a bugged room feels like, and Deneir's Sanctum felt like a gift, which is the same thing. Bookwyrm waved us into it like she was doing us a favor. "Well, you can use this room as your office to interview anyone you wish as part of your investigation, and you can rely on Fembris Lancer to catch… fetch any suspects and witnesses you wish to speak to." Catch. She said catch and corrected herself to fetch. I kept that. Daz had the same itch I did. "Do… do we think the room is, like, bugged, or has, like, secret…" He couldn't even finish it. "It's nice and all to offer up that, like, we can use the office, and that they'll go fetch people, and all of those sorts of things, but it's also a little suspect. Like, maybe they're involved, and somehow…" "It doesn't seem just friendly," Grygum said. "I mean, it could be that they genuinely want to get to the bottom of this." That's Grygum. He leaves the door open for people to be decent even while he's bolting it. This is the thing about murder among scholars. Back home — and I mean the mountain, the giants — if you wanted to know who broke a thing, you asked, and someone told you, because lying about it was beneath them. Down here, everybody's got a door they won't open. I hate it. I've always hated it. So when Bookwyrm fished — "Oh, d-do… is there any… Any suspects in particular?" — I gave her the only honest thing I had, which was nothing. "We refuse to comment on ongoing." Daz cleaned it up the way he does. "Yeah, it's an ongoing investigation, and it's not, not proper for us to share that at this time." She tried again. Asked if there was anybody we wished to start with. I shrugged at her. "We're gonna talk to anybody who might be involved, so, you know — not quite sure who we're gonna talk to next, but you shouldn't read into that." What I wanted to read into was her. "I also want to understand where Bookwyrm was before nine in the morning," I said, once we were our own again. "Timeline of where she was. So, available to be a suspect." Everyone's available until they're not. That's not cynicism. That's just keeping the list honest. Grygum was paging through our notes and frowning. "You know, there is somebody in our list of characters who seems to have the same priorities that we do. Maybe that would be someone to interview to sort of get tips on what to do next, or their suspicions." He squinted. "It isn't… for some reason, there's no name on that entry. It just says, Fheminor Scrivenbark." Our own notes had started lying to us. That felt about right for this place. Then the constraint landed — that we'd only get to chase a handful of threads before the thing moved on without us. "Sounds like bullshit," I said, because it was. "I know, but, like, why do we get it, like, what's the hurry? Investigations take as long as they take." Apparently they don't. Apparently things keep happening while you're standing around thinking. Grygum put it plainest: "There'll be more murders." So we wouldn't split, not yet. "I like us sticking together," I said. "I just think it's more imposing to have all, like, you know, five, seven, ten of us show up in a room." Grygum agreed we'd start together and peel off when two doors opened at once. We walked the council back through. The whole pack of them, shouting over a body. A'lai Aivenmore wanting a vote and new leadership. The dowdy halfling, Fheminor Scrivenbark, asking whether Janussi had named a successor. Kazryn Nyantani — slender, gray, those wrinkles around the eyes — cutting through with first you must find the murderer. The bronze dragonborn, Alkrist, formidable and furious, the gate warden needs to be dismissed, this happened on his watch. Bookwyrm trying to settle the room. And Daral not even in it — he'd been at the Hearth, asking why isn't Sylvira Savikas here. Which was the better question. Sylvira wasn't at the council. Sylvira — or somebody wearing her face — had been walking the halls in the dead of night with a lantern. "Someone impersonating her," Zalthir said. "Yes. Yes." Here's where I planted my boots. "I feel like physical evidence is more reliable than trying to parse who's lying and who's not, you know?" Down here everyone lies as a reflex. You can't out-talk a culture that talks for a living. But a smear of poison on a dead man's fingers doesn't have a motive. "But, you know, maybe that's from watching too much CSI, what do I know?" We had a sample of the stuff — off his fingers, and his lip too, Zalthir made sure of that. Grygum volunteered. "I'm happy to do the library research. Poison section, please." And Daz raised the other thread, the one nobody wanted to touch: "There's a missing part of, like, a book that should not be missing… that could have happened a hundred years ago or something, but… seems suspicious, and maybe related." Then we worked the list of people like a vein of ore, deciding where to dig. Daz took Fheminor. "I'm looking at the ones that have the least amount of time, or probably have the least amount to talk about, because sometimes those are the ones that have the most insight." Reasonable. I started down the names. "So, Bookwyrm — do we really think Bookwyrm might have done it? Do we want to give Bookwyrm the third degree?" The warning came back sharp: if we accuse her, we'd better have facts, real ones. "Right," I said, "well, we want to know, we're pretty sure, before we accuse anybody." That's the rule. You don't say the word. Not until you're sure. Daral, we crossed off — not by evidence, by gut. "It's too on the nose for it to be Daral. I don't think it's Daral." Zalthir nodded. "Reading the whole board, I don't think it's Daral." Sylvira, same logic, different reason. "Again, it's someone wore her face, is what we're talking about. I think the whole lantern aspect of it means that it probably wasn't them. She might know something, but it probably wasn't her." Which left the key. "So, I think, Kalan Strongbranch, we gotta interview." Zalthir was already there. "I'm more curious if he still has his other tower key." Two keys to the high towers. Janussi held one. "Yeah, the key is definitely a thread to pull on." Zalthir handed Daz his marching orders for Fheminor — find out when the man got beaten up, because beat-up-at-eight tells a different story than beat-up-when-he-died. Daz: "He wasn't dead yet, but was he beat up?" Zalthir: "He was beat up before he was dead." And whether the man noticed anything missing. And, Zalthir added flat as a tombstone, "if he poisoned the guy when he visited, perchance." One thing kept gnawing me, though, so I backed us up. "Kalan said they'd put the question to the corpse, and that it didn't work. And that didn't work because of Y." The imposter — the false devil-lady — supposedly did it first and locked the corpse's mouth shut for days. Maybe. "Do we know that for sure? I mean, if Kalan's just saying, hey, I did it, but didn't do it? None of us can wring words out of a dead man, so it's not like we can verify, but — whether the corpse was ever truly made to answer is hearsay." I let it sit a beat. "It's also heresy, but…"
