source_quote: Bookwyrm waved them off and ushered us in herself, all warmth, and introduced the man as Kei Tigersteel — Lorekeeper of Candlekeep, priest of the Temple of Oghma, "the library's spiritual leader."

subject: Kei Tigersteel
fact: Kei Tigersteel is the Lorekeeper of Candlekeep and priest of the Temple of Oghma, described as the library's spiritual leader; he was in confidential conference with Bookwyrm and later instructed to take the victim’s body to the Shrine of Oghma for purification.
source_quote: yes, Kei, you can take the body to the Shrine of Oghma for purification.

subject: Kei Tigersteel
fact: Kei Tigersteel is the Lorekeeper of Candlekeep, priest of the Temple of Oghma, and described as the library's spiritual leader. He was in conference with Bookwyrm when the investigators arrived, was dismissed with the directive to take the body to the Shrine of Oghma for purification, and his presence suggests a religious dimension to the investigation.
source_quote: yes, Kei, you can take the body to the Shrine of Oghma for purification.

subject: Ms. Hollypocket
fact: Ms. Hollypocket is a witness named by the investigators to placate Bookwyrm, a harmless name offered to conceal their true focus on Sylvira Savikas.
source_quote: I gave her one harmless witness to chew on, Ms. Hollypocket, whom we'd already seen anyway.

subject: number of investigators
fact: There are four investigators: Daz, Grygum, Thorin, and Zalthir.
source_quote: four, five, seven, eight, ten of us

subject: number of people at council meeting
fact: At least seven individuals are named as present at the council meeting: A'lai Aivenmore, Fheminor Scrivenbark, Kazryn Nyantani, Alkrist, Bookwyrm, Daral, and Zalthir.
source_quote: A'lai Aivenmore wanting a vote and new leadership. The dowdy halfling, Fheminor Scrivenbark, asking whether Janussi had named a successor. Kazryn Nyantani — slender, gray, those wrinkles around the eyes — cutting through with first you must find the murderer. The bronze dragonborn, Alkrist, formidable and furious... Bookwyrm trying to settle the room. And Daral not even in it

subject: Quiet Ink-Stained Brother
fact: A silent, unnamed brother in the Shadow Monks’ order, remembered for ink-stained hands and participation in silent communication training, but Zalthir cannot confirm his role or presence.
source_quote: I think it was Brother Heslin... or possibly the quiet one with the ink-stained hands.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira is referenced by Daral Yashenti as the 'horned tart' who was the object of Janussi's affections, and whose horns Daral emphasized as the relevant fact when speaking of her.
source_quote: That's — Sylvira." He said it like the horns were the relevant fact.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira was referenced by Daral as Janussi's 'horned tart,' revealing his bias against non-drow figures through the same linguistic register drow use to dismiss outsiders.
source_quote: That's — Sylvira. He said it like the horns were the relevant fact.

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas is a figure whose identity was impersonated by someone wearing her face and carrying a lantern in the dead of night, prompting Bookwyrm’s unstated preference for the investigation to focus on her.
source_quote: Someone had impersonated Sylvira — Grygum thought it made perfect sense, and tactically it did, the impersonated woman might know who would wear her face.

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas is a high-ranking figure in Candlekeep whose identity was impersonated by an unknown individual seen walking the halls at night with a lantern; Bookwyrm’s unstated desire to direct the investigation toward her suggests Sylvira may be central to the truth — or a red herring.
source_quote: Someone impersonating her... Yes. Yes.

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas is a missing scholar whose identity has been impersonated; someone wearing her face was seen walking the halls at night with a lantern, and she was absent from the council meeting despite being central to the investigation.
source_quote: Daral not even in it — he'd been at the Hearth, asking why isn't Sylvira Savikas here.

subject: Teles
fact: Teles is referenced by Daral Yashenti as a deluded old git among the suspects in Janussi’s death.
source_quote: Teles, the deluded old git;

subject: Teles
fact: Teles was identified by Daral as a deluded old git who wanted the top job, and thus a potential suspect in Janussi's death.
source_quote: Teles, the deluded old git;

subject: the former shadow monk
fact: The former shadow monk is referenced by Zalthir as the one who observed the exchange between Zalthir and Glabbagool and remarked that Zalthir would have understood Glabbagool’s answer if he had paid attention to the silent communication class.
source_quote: The former shadow monk had been watching the whole exchange. He looked at me and said that if I had paid more attention to the classes on silent communication, I would know exactly what Glabbagool's answer meant.

subject: the narrator
fact: The narrator is a persistent, observant figure who tracks behavioral patterns, recognizes linguistic biases, and deduces truth through physical details — notably the act of finger-licking on book pages.
source_quote: I watched the finger go to the mouth and back to the paper. I was fairly sure I knew what I was watching.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin and his wife have watched the entire Poirot series and are saving the last episode.
source_quote: "My wife and I have watched the entire series, and we're down to the last episode, and we're saving it. I'm not sure for why, but —"

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes Bookwyrm might be the murderer, though he doesn't think she is.
source_quote: "I'm just saying, like, if Bookwyrm ended up doing it, which I don't think she did, but… then."

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes the person who killed the victim is the one who took the heart, because everything else is just people talking and the heart is a fact.
source_quote: "Right, but at the end of the day, I'm pretty sure that the person that killed him is the one that took the heart," I said. Everything else is people talking. The heart is a fact.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes the room in Deneir's Sanctum feels like a gift, implying he distrusts the offer.
source_quote: I have spent enough time in the Underdark to know what a bugged room feels like, and Deneir's Sanctum felt like a gift, which is the same thing.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin considers Bookwyrm a suspect and wants to know her whereabouts before nine in the morning.
source_quote: "I also want to understand where Bookwyrm was before nine in the morning," I said, once we were our own again. "Timeline of where she was. So, available to be a suspect."

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin considers the theory that Daral killed Janussi because he finally got rid of someone holding him back.
source_quote: A cleaner theory. Possibly the correct one.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin does not argue when Kalan calls the investigators outsiders who were hired to bungle the case.
source_quote: Thorin, to his credit, didn't argue the insult. "I don't doubt that maybe they hired us because they thought we were gonna screw it up."

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin doubts whether the corpse was ever truly made to answer, calling it hearsay and heresy.
source_quote: "Do we know that for sure? I mean, if Kalan's just saying, hey, I did it, but didn't do it? None of us can wring words out of a dead man, so it's not like we can verify, but — whether the corpse was ever truly made to answer is hearsay." I let it sit a beat. "It's also heresy, but…"

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin hates the bureaucratic apparatus of Candlekeep.
source_quote: Thorin — who hates the whole rotten apparatus of who-knows-what — put the obvious crack in it before I had to.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin intends to keep Daral under close watch until midnight to test if he is the poisoner.
source_quote: We'd keep Daral close until midnight — a cleric who could draw poison out, and a sword that could do the same, both within arm's reach.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a giant-raised investigator who cuts through pretense to ask direct questions about authority and power. He is the one who first asked who the investigators work for, and who insisted the crime scene remain sealed. He refused to name suspects, citing protocol, and is wary of the library’s institutional structure.
source_quote: We refuse to comment on ongoing.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a giant-raised investigator who distrusts deception and favors blunt, physical evidence; he insists on sticking together as a group for intimidation, questions Bookwyrm’s timeline, and refuses to name suspects until verified.
source_quote: We refuse to comment on ongoing.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a giant-raised investigator who distrusts deception, insists on physical evidence, and demands clarity on timelines and authority, including Bookwyrm’s whereabouts before the murder.
source_quote: I also want to understand where Bookwyrm was before nine in the morning... Timeline of where she was. So, available to be a suspect.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is referenced as the speaker who says, 'Right, but at the end of the day, I'm pretty sure that the person that killed him is the one that took the heart,' and later asserts that the heart is a fact.
source_quote: Right, but at the end of the day, I'm pretty sure that the person that killed him is the one that took the heart," I said. Everything else is people talking. The heart is a fact.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is the lead interrogator who methodically dismantles Daral’s narratives using contradiction, psychological pressure, and forensic logic. He identifies the book as the vector of poison and confronts Daral with the physical evidence — the finger-wiping pattern. He maintains control of the interrogation and insists on evidence collection.
source_quote: We did want to take it into evidence.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is the lead investigator on the ground, experienced in the Underdark, deeply suspicious of deception, and insists on maintaining a neutral stance while probing Bookwyrm’s alibi and the team’s own contradictory notes.
source_quote: I also want to understand where Bookwyrm was before nine in the morning… Everyone's available until they're not.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noticed Bookwyrm corrected 'catch' to 'fetch' and kept that detail in mind.
source_quote: Catch. She said catch and corrected herself to fetch. I kept that.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin questioned Kalan about the High Tower’s security, the nature of the key, and whether it had been compromised; he pushed for metaphysical explanations — including daylight savings and time zones — regarding the midnight poison; he accepted that the tower’s constant surveillance rendered Kalan’s access unverifiable; he later recognized the significance of the two-handed search pattern and the discrepancy between the locket-key and the safe-rifling.
source_quote: The tower is watched. Always. People stand at it whether the key is in someone's pocket or not.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin questioned the metaphysical implications of the poison's timing, particularly regarding time zones and astronomical midnight, and identified the key detail that saliva darkens the otherwise pale ochre dust.
source_quote: What darkens it is saliva. The ochre reacts on contact with spit, and a man turning pages licks his fingers to do it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin refuses to comment on suspects during the investigation.
source_quote: "We refuse to comment on ongoing."

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin thinks physical evidence is more reliable than trying to parse lies.
source_quote: "I feel like physical evidence is more reliable than trying to parse who's lying and who's not, you know?"

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin thinks real detectives write everything down.
source_quote: "I think real detectives just write everything down."

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wants to know if the High Tower has been compromised and whether Kalan himself might have used the key to enter it.
source_quote: Thorin wanted to know if it had been compromised — whether Kalan himself might have used the key, walked in, walked out.

subject: Vooshadi Moonriver
fact: Vooshadi Moonriver is a scribe assigned to guard the door of Deneir's Sanctum, the investigators' temporary office. Their role is to prevent unauthorized entry, reinforcing the controlled access to the investigation space.
source_quote: Vooshadi Moonriver would stand the door — we wouldn't want anyone the investigators don't want to come in, to come in.

subject: Vooshadi Moonriver
fact: Vooshadi Moonriver is assigned to guard the door of Deneir's Sanctum, with explicit instructions to prevent unauthorized individuals from entering.
source_quote: Vooshadi Moonriver would stand the door — "we wouldn't want anyone the investigators don't want to come in, to come in."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir acknowledges he has slept through many important lessons.
source_quote: There are, by now, a great many days I was sleeping.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes Daral is not the murderer.
source_quote: Zalthir nodded. "Reading the whole board, I don't think it's Daral."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes Kalan chose Grygum to receive the key deliberately, not by chance.
source_quote: The key went to Grygum. I marked that before anything else — not into Daz's hand, not into Thorin's, not into the open air for whoever was closest. Kalan stepped out of a doorway we hadn't clocked... He chose the orc. I don't think it was chance.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes Kalan is a good investigator who is being deliberately sidelined and that his own team has already outperformed him.
source_quote: "Is he aware that someone was pretending to be Sylvira Savikas the night of the murder?" He went still. "No. That is new information." A pause. "You are very good at this."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes it is unlikely Sylvira herself committed the murder because someone wore her face.
source_quote: "Again, it's someone wore her face, is what we're talking about. I think the whole lantern aspect of it means that it probably wasn't them. She might know something, but it probably wasn't her."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes someone impersonated Sylvira Savikas.
source_quote: "Someone impersonating her," Zalthir said. "Yes. Yes."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir confronted Kalan about the key’s transfer, the murder’s timing, and the possibility of deception; he challenged Kalan’s assumption that the safe-rifling and the heart removal were committed by the same person, exposing a flaw in the theory; he obtained confirmation that Kalan could perform truth-detection magic if needed; he revealed new information about a shapeshifter impersonating Sylvira Savikas, which stunned Kalan and shifted the investigation’s direction.
source_quote: Is he aware that someone was pretending to be Sylvira Savikas the night of the murder?

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir expected a time-freezing spell from the sapphire inscription and was disappointed to discover it was a summoning spell, revealing his bias toward temporal magic over retrieval magic.
source_quote: Zalthir had been expecting a working that freezes a thing in stopped time, and seemed almost disappointed.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir feels excitement about Glabbagool’s abilities and his new form.
source_quote: This is exciting. We formed Voltron or something.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir instructs Daz to investigate whether Fheminor was beaten before death and whether he poisoned the victim.
source_quote: Zalthir handed Daz his marching orders for Fheminor — find out when the man got beaten up, because beat-up-at-eight tells a different story than beat-up-when-he-died. Daz: "He wasn't dead yet, but was he beat up?" Zalthir: "He was beat up before he was dead." And whether the man noticed anything missing. And, Zalthir added flat as a tombstone, "if he poisoned the guy when he visited, perchance."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir intends to keep checking on the drow in the bag of holding, as Glabbagool reminded him.
source_quote: Well, either way, as long as you check in on the drow, we're all good.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a former shadow monk who has been permanently bonded to Glabbagool, an ooze entity. He lacks understanding of silent communication and was absent during the class where Glabbagool’s wisdom was taught. He is emotionally detached, pragmatic, and reacts with excitement to his new abilities, despite his ignorance of deeper philosophical contexts.
source_quote: I liked it." "This is exciting.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a former student who missed the lesson on silent communication, now bonded with Glabbagool, a transformed shadow monk, and carries four eyes on his forearm that he considers part of himself.
source_quote: I liked it. Then he added that it must be quiet, and I liked that more. "Well, good! So I just admire him now."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a participant in a secret meeting with Kalan, where he challenges Grygum’s assumptions about the murder and safe-rifling, and proposes collaboration after revealing new information about Sylvira Savikas being impersonated.
source_quote: I gave him the *okay* and let it sit.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is an investigator who collected poison samples from the victim’s fingers and lip, and who advised Daz to determine whether Fheminor Scrivenbark was beaten before or after death.
source_quote: Zalthir made sure of that... Zalthir: "He was beat up before he was dead." And whether the man noticed anything missing. And, Zalthir added flat as a tombstone, "if he poisoned the guy when he visited, perchance."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is an investigator who collected poison samples from the victim’s fingers and lips, advocated for physical evidence over testimony, and assigned Daz to investigate Fheminor Scrivenbark’s injuries and potential poisoning.
source_quote: I'm happy to do the library research. Poison section, please.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is referenced by himself as the one who failed to learn the lesson of silent communication in the class taught by Brother Heslin or the ink-stained quiet one, and who now carries Glabbagool as a sentient companion bonded to his arm.
source_quote: I did not understand it. ... I think it was Brother Heslin, the one who always smelled of incense, or possibly the quiet one with the ink-stained hands. Silent discussion. Communication without sound. I remember the light through the shutters. I do not remember the lesson.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is the first to openly acknowledge the impersonation of Sylvira Savikas, affirming its plausibility and tactical advantage — indicating he is tracking the deception closely.
source_quote: Someone impersonating her," Zalthir said. "Yes. Yes.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is the one who suspects the murderer is a magic user capable of talking locks open, notices the heart was removed post-mortem to prevent resurrection, and later deduces that the murderer may have been mistaken for the safe-rifler.
source_quote: He noticed the heart hacked out — after death, to spoil resurrection. ... He noticed the murderer was a magic user who could circumvent arcane and mundane locks. Magic that could talk any lock open, arcane or iron, the very highest order of that art. ... He assumed the murderer was the one who opened the safe. I stopped him. ... Two hands had searched that apartment — one that knew exactly where to look, one that didn't.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir prefers that Glabbagool blend into his scales rather than appear as a separate creature with obvious eyes.
source_quote: I suggested he might not need them — that he could blend into me rather than read as a separate creature riding along.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realizes Glabbagool mastered the lesson of stillness that he himself failed to learn.
source_quote: The student on my arm had mastered the one lesson I most thoroughly missed, and he had done it in under a minute, by going still.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realizes Kalan was hasty in assuming the murderer was the one who rifled the safe, and corrects him by pointing out the key was in the locket.
source_quote: I stopped him. The key was in the locket. The locket was around the keeper's neck. The locket was gone. So why would the killer go through the safe at all?

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recalls attending a class on silent communication but cannot remember the lesson.
source_quote: I remember the light through the shutters. I do not remember the lesson.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir suspects Kalan is being set up to fail and that the real凶手 is being protected by Bookwyrm or someone else.
source_quote: He suspected, he said, was that one of the Great Readers was the murderer, and that either Bookwyrm was protecting them or someone had convinced her to fire him to protect themselves.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir tells Kalan they are only there because someone put them up to it and they are happy to not get involved — and believes this to be true.
source_quote: "Purely accidental," I told him. "We have no particular involvement here. Someone put us up to this. We are happy to not get involved." True enough. Filed under things that are also true.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thinks Kalan is at risk of being killed over a key he no longer has and warns him to watch his back because shapeshifters exist.
source_quote: "Given that you're at risk of being killed over a key you don't have anymore, watch your back," I told him. "Keep in mind there are people who can change their form. Shapeshift. Whatever you want to call it."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir wishes the Whispering Dome were quiet and undisturbed, as he has spent his life seeking such spaces.
source_quote: The Whispering Dome was the kind of place I would have liked under different circumstances. Quiet. Low light pooling under the curve of the ceiling. No one talking unless they had a reason. I have spent most of my life looking for rooms like this, and most of my life finding them already occupied by people who would not stop making noise.

subject: Bag of Holding
fact: The bag of holding contains drow who require monitoring, and Glabbagool’s first act after transformation was to remind Zalthir of this responsibility.
source_quote: Before he settled in, he reminded me the drow in the bag of holding still needed watching.

subject: blackened finger
fact: The victim’s finger was blackened due to contact between midnight tears and saliva, indicating he licked his fingers while reading the poisoned book.
source_quote: Some liquid had gotten onto his finger, and the finger had gone black. ... The dust stays pale ochre. What darkens it is saliva. ... His fingers were black, his lips were black, and he died at midnight.

subject: book of Oghma
fact: The book of Oghma is referenced as the spiritual authority guiding Kei Tigersteel, whose role as priest of the Temple of Oghma implies the book's centrality to purification rites.
source_quote: Kei Tigersteel — Lorekeeper of Candlekeep, priest of the Temple of Oghma, "the library's spiritual leader."

subject: brass key
fact: The brass key is the second key to the High Tower, previously held by Kalan Strongbranch, and was physically transferred into Grygum's palm.
source_quote: pressed a small brass key specifically into the cleric's palm.

subject: drow overseer count
fact: Drow in the context of prisoner labor are overseers, not workers.
source_quote: Drow named in connection with prisoner labor are overseers, not workers.

subject: false devil-lady
fact: The false devil-lady is a figure referenced by Kalan Strongbranch as having locked the corpse’s mouth shut, preventing interrogation — a claim that may be false or heretical.
source_quote: Kalan said they'd put the question to the corpse, and that it didn't work. And that didn't work because of Y. The imposter — the false devil-lady — supposedly did it first and locked the corpse's mouth shut for days.

subject: Fey-mous Flowers & Fungi
fact: The book *Fey-mous Flowers & Fungi* by Archibald Roots, Jr. contains the formula for midnight tears and its antidotal transformation into a pain-relief solution, and was the physical vector of the poison used in the murder.
source_quote: The book was the murder weapon, and he'd read himself dead.

subject: glabbagool eyes count
fact: Glabbagool has four eyes on Zalthir’s arm, which Zalthir later requested to blend into his scales.
source_quote: Four, as it turned out, blinking up from my own scales... Maybe he can just look more like my normal — scales, whatever I have.

subject: imposter's face
fact: An imposter wore the face of Sylvira Savikas, enabling unauthorized nocturnal access to restricted areas of Candlekeep.
source_quote: Someone had impersonated Sylvira — Grygum thought it made perfect sense, and tactically it did, the impersonated woman might know who would wear her face.

subject: investigation log
fact: The investigators' own log has begun to omit or falsify information, as evidenced by the blank entry for Fheminor Scrivenbark.
source_quote: Our own notes had started lying to us.

subject: Janussi’s key
fact: Janussi’s key is suspected to have been placed in the locket as a false clue, possibly by the impersonator or an accomplice to mislead investigators.
source_quote: The locket could just as easily be Janussi's key, handed off by a man building a clean story.

subject: key carry definition
fact: Worn objects are not considered 'carried' for the purpose of the sapphire summoning spell.
source_quote: It doesn't, as it turned out. Which reframed the whole use.

subject: Lantern
fact: A lantern was carried by the impersonator of Sylvira Savikas during nighttime movements, indicating premeditation and a need for illumination — possibly to access hidden areas or signal others.
source_quote: Sylvira — or somebody wearing her face — had been walking the halls in the dead of night with a lantern.

subject: lantern
fact: A lantern was carried by the impersonator of Sylvira Savikas during nocturnal movements in the library, marking the first visible trace of the imposter.
source_quote: Sylvira — or somebody wearing her face — had been walking the halls in the dead of night with a lantern.

subject: lantern ownership
fact: A lantern was carried by the impersonator of Sylvira Savikas during nighttime movements.
source_quote: Sylvira — or somebody wearing her face — had been walking the halls in the dead of night with a lantern

subject: locket
fact: The locket is a container previously used to carry the High Tower key, worn around the victim’s neck, and now missing, raising doubt over whether Kalan’s demonstration locket is genuine or Janussi’s.
source_quote: The key was in the locket. The locket was around the keeper's neck. The locket was gone. ... Kalan pulled out his own locket to demonstrate the method of carry. ... So we asked him to open it and show us. ... The locket was missing. The key was in the missing locket.

subject: Locket-key
fact: The High Tower key was stored inside a locket worn around Janussi’s neck; the locket was stolen after the murder, removing the only physical proof of the key’s location; Kalan demonstrated a similar locket to prove the method of concealment, but his version was empty, casting doubt on his story.
source_quote: The locket was missing. The key was in the missing locket.

subject: Locket-Key
fact: The locket-key, hidden on the victim’s person, was known to only one of the two individuals who stood over the body — the other tore through the safe instead, suggesting targeted theft.
source_quote: One who knew exactly where the locket-key hid, and one who didn't and tore through the safe instead.

subject: locket key storage
fact: The key was carried in a locket worn around the neck, now missing.
source_quote: The key was in the locket. The locket was around the keeper's neck. The locket was gone.

subject: midnight tears
fact: Midnight tears is a highly toxic pale ochre dust derived from Feywild pollen, lethal when ingested, and causes death precisely at midnight unless neutralized with specific Feywild sap.
source_quote: Midnight tears. A highly toxic pale ochre dust, made from the pollen of a plant usually found only in the Feywild. ... When midnight tears are mixed with the sap of a certain Feywild tree, they lose their toxicity entirely ... Otherwise: lethal. ... The creature that ingests this poison suffers no effect until the stroke of midnight.

subject: midnight tears
fact: Midnight tears is a pale ochre Feywild dust derived from pollen of a plant found only in the Feywild; it remains non-lethal until mixed with the sap of a specific Feywild tree, and becomes lethal upon contact with saliva.
source_quote: When midnight tears are mixed with the sap of a certain Feywild tree, they lose their toxicity entirely and become a powerful pain-relief solution... Otherwise: lethal. Food or liquid, either delivery worked.

subject: Midnight tears
fact: Midnight tears is a pale ochre, highly toxic dust derived from Feywild pollen; it is inert until midnight, at which point it kills the victim; it darkens upon contact with saliva, indicating ingestion via licked fingers; it is extremely rare, accessible only to those with Feywild connections.
source_quote: The black stuff, yes, we saw that.

subject: midnight tears poison origin
fact: Midnight tears is a highly toxic pale ochre dust made from Feywild pollen, lethal unless neutralized by specific Feywild sap.
source_quote: A highly toxic pale ochre dust, made from the pollen of a plant usually found only in the Feywild.

subject: Missing Book Fragment
fact: A fragment of a book is missing — possibly removed a century ago — and is suspected to be connected to the murders; its absence suggests a hidden ritual, forbidden knowledge, or an ancient cover-up.
source_quote: There's a missing part of, like, a book that should not be missing… that could have happened a hundred years ago or something, but… seems suspicious.

subject: missing book fragment
fact: A fragment of a book is missing, possibly unrelated to the current murder but deemed suspicious and potentially connected by Daz.
source_quote: There's a missing part of, like, a book that should not be missing… that could have happened a hundred years ago or something, but… seems suspicious, and maybe related.

subject: poisoned book
fact: The poisoned book was the delivery mechanism for midnight tears, with the poison activated by the victim’s saliva as he licked his fingers while reading, leading to his death at midnight.
source_quote: So somebody doped up the book. ... His fingers were black, his lips were black, and he died at midnight. The book was the murder weapon, and he'd read himself dead.

subject: poisoned book value
fact: The book used to carry poison was one of Daral's favorite volumes, licked by the killer.
source_quote: The poison carried on a book, transferred by a man licking his finger and turning the pages.

subject: poison sample
fact: A sample of poison was collected from the victim’s fingers and lip by Zalthir, and is being analyzed for identification.
source_quote: We had a sample of the stuff — off his fingers, and his lip too, Zalthir made sure of that.

subject: Poison Sample
fact: A sample of poison was collected from the victim’s fingers and lips by Zalthir; it is the only physical evidence available, and its origin is unknown — potentially linked to the missing book fragment or the impersonation of Sylvira.
source_quote: Off his fingers, and his lip too, Zalthir made sure of that.

subject: poison sample value
fact: A sample of poison was taken from the victim's fingers and lip, but no monetary value is assigned.
source_quote: a sample of the stuff — off his fingers, and his lip too

subject: sapphire spell function
fact: The sapphire summoning spell retrieves a hidden object to the caster's hand, regardless of location.
source_quote: You can put it someplace, you can throw it into a river or whatever. Nobody will find it, and then when you need it back, boom.

subject: Sapphire summoning spell
fact: A rare arcane working that allows the caster to summon a specific object into their hand from anywhere it has been hidden; requires a very expensive sapphire as a focus; does not function on objects worn, only carried; enables concealment of the High Tower key by storing it in a distant, inaccessible location and retrieving it only at the moment of use.
source_quote: This would be great for the High Tower Keys.

subject: Sapphire summoning spell
fact: The sapphire summoning spell is an ancient enchantment that recalls a single object to the caster’s hand, requiring an expensive sapphire and functioning regardless of whether the object is carried or hidden.
source_quote: You can put it someplace, you can throw it into a river or whatever. Nobody will find it, and then when you need it back, boom.

subject: Sapphire summoning spell
fact: The sapphire summoning spell is an ancient working that allows a hidden object to be summoned back into the caster’s hand, requiring a very expensive sapphire, and does not function if the object is worn.
source_quote: It's an old summoning working — the kind that calls a single hidden thing back into your hand. ... It needs a very expensive sapphire. ... You can put it someplace, you can throw it into a river or whatever. Nobody will find it, and then when you need it back, boom.

subject: Second High Tower Key
fact: The second key to the High Tower, previously held by Kalan Strongbranch, was secretly given to Grygum; its current location is unknown to all but Grygum and Kalan.
source_quote: I have given it now to someone who is not me.

subject: silver candlestick value
fact: The silver candlesticks flanking the Lolth altar are worth 25 gp each.
source_quote: a pair of heavy silver candlesticks worth 25 gp each

subject: the bag of holding
fact: The bag of holding contains captured drow, whose monitoring is a responsibility Glabbagool insists upon even in the moment of his own transformation. It represents unresolved threats and the continuity of duty — a reminder that even in transcendence, obligations remain. It is a key element in Glabbagool’s pragmatic nature.
source_quote: The drow in the bag of holding still needed watching.

subject: the body
fact: The body of the murder victim has been identified and is awaiting purification at the Shrine of Oghma. Its handling by Kei Tigersteel suggests it is a key piece of evidence with religious significance, and its removal from the chapter house marks the transition from crime scene to ritual space.
source_quote: the body went to be purified.

subject: the book
fact: The book is referenced by Zalthir as the object on which poison was carried, transferred by a man licking his finger and turning the pages, and which Daral Yashenti had given to Janussi as a lesson in worth, later found in his possession.
source_quote: The book had been in his collection for years, he said. One of his favorites. He'd given it away to make a point — that his books should never be sold — by having Janussi read it and understand their worth.

subject: the book
fact: The book was a favorite of Daral's, given to Janussi as a symbolic gesture to teach the value of tomes, later found to be the poisoned vector; Daral licked his fingers while turning its pages, and the book was seized as evidence.
source_quote: We took it. We'd keep Daral close until midnight... The dead poisoner is the innocent one.

subject: the locket
fact: The locket, once worn by the victim, contained the key to the safe — now missing — and is suspected of being used as a decoy or to mislead investigators, possibly containing Janussi’s key instead.
source_quote: The key was in the missing locket.

subject: the poisoned book
fact: The poisoned book was a personal favorite of Daral Yashenti, given to Janussi as a symbolic lesson on the value of sacred texts. It became the vector of death when Daral licked its pages during emotional turmoil, transferring poison through finger contact. It was later used by Daral to distract and mislead investigators, and it was seized as evidence by Thorin.
source_quote: He wet his finger and began flicking through the pages.

subject: the poison in the left hand
fact: A poison was detected in the left hand of the victim, noted by Kalan as a deliberate clue, possibly linked to botanical sources now under investigation in the Flora Theca.
source_quote: He had noticed the poison in the left hand, the saliva.

subject: tower key
fact: There are two keys to the high towers; one was held by the deceased Janussi, and the other is suspected to be in the possession of Kalan Strongbranch.
source_quote: Two keys to the high towers. Janussi held one. "Yeah, the key is definitely a thread to pull on."

subject: Tower Key
fact: Two keys grant access to Candlekeep’s high towers; one was held by the victim Janussi, the other by Kalan Strongbranch; the key’s current location is unknown and may reveal who had access to the murder scene.
source_quote: I'm more curious if he still has his other tower key.

subject: Blending vs. Visibility
fact: Zalthir proposes Glabbagool should blend into his scales rather than appear as a separate creature, challenging the expectation that bonded entities must be visibly distinct.
source_quote: I suggested he might not need them — that he could blend into me rather than read as a separate creature riding along.

subject: Bookwyrm's alibi
fact: Thorin wants to verify Bookwyrm's whereabouts before nine in the morning to determine if she could be a suspect.
source_quote: "I also want to understand where Bookwyrm was before nine in the morning," I said, once we were our own again. "Timeline of where she was. So, available to be a suspect."

subject: Bookwyrm’s alibi before 9 a.m.
fact: Thorin is pursuing Bookwyrm’s whereabouts before 9 a.m. as a critical unresolved thread — her accessibility as a suspect remains unverified, and her actions during that window may reveal involvement.
source_quote: I also want to understand where Bookwyrm was before nine in the morning…

subject: Bookwyrm’s motives
fact: Bookwyrm’s decision to fire Kalan is a lingering mystery — whether it was to protect a Great Reader, sabotage the investigation, or cover up her own involvement.
source_quote: I believe you're only being employed so you're likely to bungle the case...

subject: Bookwyrm’s true allegiance
fact: Bookwyrm’s role in the investigation is ambiguous; she may be protecting the murderer, being manipulated by them, or acting to contain a greater threat; Kalan believes she ordered his removal to silence him; Zalthir suspects she is part of the conspiracy, and the team’s employment may be a cover to mislead the real investigators.
source_quote: You're only being employed so you're likely to bungle the case.

subject: Bookwyrm’s True Motives
fact: Bookwyrm’s intense, unspoken focus on Sylvira Savikas as the primary suspect suggests she may be attempting to divert attention from herself or another powerful figure; her offer of assistance may be a means of control.
source_quote: She never said it. She didn't have to; the want came off her like heat off the smelters.

subject: Bookwyrm’s true role
fact: It is unknown whether Bookwyrm is the investigator’s superior, the perpetrator, or something else entirely. Her excessive generosity, rapid questioning about suspects, and control over access to information raise suspicion. The investigators note she is 'not above suspicion' and the possibility that she may be involved makes the investigation potentially 'awkward.'
source_quote: I'm just saying, like, if Bookwyrm ended up doing it, which I don't think she did, but… then. This could get awkward.

subject: carried vs. worn objects
fact: The distinction between 'carried' and 'worn' objects affects the functionality of the sapphire summoning spell, with the spell not activating on items worn (like lanyards), reframing its tactical use.
source_quote: Whether a thing worn counts as a thing carried. 'I would think so. I'd think that you're carrying anything that you're wearing.' It doesn't, as it turned out.

subject: corpse interrogation claim
fact: Kalan claimed they tried to question the corpse, but it didn't work because the mouth was locked shut.
source_quote: Kalan said they'd put the question to the corpse, and that it didn't work. And that didn't work because of Y. The imposter — the false devil-lady — supposedly did it first and locked the corpse's mouth shut for days.

subject: Daral's admission of confusion
fact: Daral claimed he was drugged and upset, suggesting his actions were not deliberate — but his repeated finger-licking and book-handling contradicted this, pointing to intentional poisoning.
source_quote: I was drugged. I was upset. I don't know what I was thinking.

subject: Eyes on Forearm
fact: Glabbagool manifests four eyes on Zalthir’s forearm, and Zalthir debates whether they should appear as separate entities or blend into his natural scales to avoid detection.
source_quote: Four, as it turned out, blinking up from my own scales. "Well, good! So I just admire him now."

subject: False Devil-Lady Imposter
fact: An imposter wearing the guise of a devil-lady is suspected of having silenced the corpse, making it impossible to verify whether the victim ever answered questions — this claim is unverified and possibly fabricated by Kalan.
source_quote: The imposter — the false devil-lady — supposedly did it first and locked the corpse's mouth shut for days. Maybe.

subject: Fheminor Scrivenbark's beating
fact: Zalthir wants to know whether Fheminor was beaten before death and whether he poisoned the victim.
source_quote: Zalthir handed Daz his marching orders for Fheminor — find out when the man got beaten up, because beat-up-at-eight tells a different story than beat-up-when-he-died. Daz: "He wasn't dead yet, but was he beat up?" Zalthir: "He was beat up before he was dead." And whether the man noticed anything missing. And, Zalthir added flat as a tombstone, "if he poisoned the guy when he visited, perchance."

subject: Glabbagool's transformation
fact: Glabbagool and Zalthir are now permanently bound, with Glabbagool settling on Zalthir’s arm and integrating with his physiology.
source_quote: Glabbagool and Zalthir, together now, he said, settling along my forearm like he had measured it in advance.

subject: Heart of the Victim
fact: The victim's heart was removed; it is considered the only concrete fact in the investigation, with all other details being hearsay or deception — the killer is presumed to be the one who took it.
source_quote: I'm pretty sure that the person that killed him is the one that took the heart.

subject: identity of the killer
fact: The investigators have formed opinions on potential suspects based on perceived motivation or external accusations, but refuse to disclose them. The nature of the suspects, their connections to Candlekeep’s hierarchy, and the timing of the murders remain undisclosed, creating a central mystery.
source_quote: We have a couple suspects that we would like to pursue, due to perceiving that they may have a motivation...

subject: impersonation thread
fact: Someone impersonated Sylvira Savikas, walking the halls at night with a lantern.
source_quote: Someone impersonating her

subject: Kalan's Disappearance
fact: Kalan Strongbranch has warned that if he does not appear the next day, he should not be sought at his post — implying he expects to be killed and is preparing for his own death.
source_quote: If I and I do not see you tomorrow, do not look for me at my post.

subject: Kalan’s trustworthiness
fact: Kalan’s credibility is in question — his assumptions are contradicted, his timeline compromised by impersonation, and his removal from the case may have been orchestrated to silence him.
source_quote: You are very good at this.

subject: magic vs. mundane timekeeping
fact: The magical nature of midnight tears’ activation defies conventional timekeeping, leaving open whether it responds to celestial, local, or intrinsic magical time — a mystery unresolved by all present.
source_quote: How do they account for daylight savings time? Did you ever… an astronomical midnight?

subject: missing book fragment thread
fact: A missing part of a book, possibly from a hundred years ago, is noted as suspicious and potentially related.
source_quote: There's a missing part of, like, a book that should not be missing… that could have happened a hundred years ago or something

subject: Missing Book Part
fact: A missing fragment of a book is considered a potential clue, possibly linked to ancient magic or the murder, but its relevance is speculative and unconfirmed.
source_quote: There's a missing part of, like, a book that should not be missing… that could have happened a hundred years ago or something, but… seems suspicious.

subject: Missing Silent Communication Lesson
fact: Zalthir missed the critical lesson on silent communication, a gap now exploited by Glabbagool, who mastered it in under a minute by going still, leaving Zalthir unable to interpret the monk’s wisdom.
source_quote: That, apparently, had been the day I was sleeping. "Too much gardening research."

subject: origin of the key
fact: The origin of the key — whether it belonged to Janussi, the victim, or was planted — is unclear, and its presence in the locket may be a deliberate misdirection.
source_quote: The locket could just as easily be Janussi's key, handed off by a man building a clean story.

subject: poisoned book vector
fact: The poison was carried on a book and transferred by licking fingers while turning pages — a method confirmed by Thorin, making Daral’s own behavior the critical clue in identifying the true poisoner.
source_quote: Janussi had been poisoned, the poison carried on a book, transferred by a man licking his finger and turning the pages.

subject: surveillance in Deneir's Sanctum
fact: The investigators suspect their private office may be bugged or monitored, despite Bookwyrm’s assurances of privacy. The offer of an unguarded space, coupled with the requirement to be escorted everywhere else in Candlekeep, creates a paradox that implies the office may be the only place under observation.
source_quote: Do we think the room is, like, bugged... or does the stuff we do in there is actually going to be private to us?

subject: The corpse's mouth being locked
fact: Thorin doubts whether the corpse was ever truly made to answer, calling it hearsay and heresy.
source_quote: "Do we know that for sure? I mean, if Kalan's just saying, hey, I did it, but didn't do it? None of us can wring words out of a dead man, so it's not like we can verify, but — whether the corpse was ever truly made to answer is hearsay." I let it sit a beat. "It's also heresy, but…"

subject: The Corpse’s Silence
fact: Kalan Strongbranch claims the corpse was prevented from answering questions — a claim that cannot be verified and may be a lie to conceal his own failure or involvement; the possibility that the corpse was never truly questioned remains a heretical doubt.
source_quote: Whether the corpse was ever truly made to answer is hearsay.

subject: the identity of the poisoner
fact: The thread of who poisoned Janussi remains formally unresolved, but all evidence points to Daral Yashenti — the only person who consistently handled the book with his fingers, expressed rage over its contents, and exhibited the physical behavior (licking pages) that enabled transfer. His alibi of intoxication and his deflection toward others are narrative tactics, not proof of innocence.
source_quote: The dead poisoner is the innocent one.

subject: The Impersonation of Sylvira
fact: The identity of the person impersonating Sylvira Savikas remains unknown; the impersonator’s nighttime movements with a lantern, combined with the locked corpse, suggest a ritualistic or magical purpose tied to forbidden knowledge.
source_quote: Sylvira — or somebody wearing her face — had been walking the halls in the dead of night with a lantern.

subject: The missing book fragment
fact: Daz suspects the missing part of a book may be connected to the murder.
source_quote: "There's a missing part of, like, a book that should not be missing… that could have happened a hundred years ago or something, but… seems suspicious, and maybe related."

subject: The Poison and the Missing Book
fact: The poison used to kill Janussi may be derived from a forbidden text whose fragment is missing; the connection between the book and the poison could reveal an ancient heresy or a cult operating within Candlekeep.
source_quote: Maybe that's from watching too much CSI, what do I know?

subject: time zone ambiguity
fact: The magical timing of midnight tears' lethality remains unexplained in terms of real-world timekeeping, with no consensus on whether it follows local, astronomical, or magical midnight.
source_quote: Nobody had an answer for the time zones. 'It's magic,' I said. That covers most of it.

subject: tower key thread
fact: Kalan Strongbranch may still possess his other tower key, a key thread to pursue.
source_quote: I'm more curious if he still has his other tower key

subject: true identity of the murderer
fact: The true identity of the murderer remains unresolved, with conflicting theories: one person who bypassed locks and planted clues, or two separate actors — one killer and one who rifled the safe.
source_quote: Perhaps it was two different people.

subject: Voltron Reference
fact: Zalthir misinterprets Glabbagool’s bonding as resembling a pop-culture fusion entity (Voltron), revealing his disconnect from the monastic wisdom and reliance on vernacular analogies.
source_quote: "This is exciting. We formed Voltron or something."

subject: who hired Zalthir and Kalan
fact: It is implied that Zalthir and Kalan were hired not to solve the case, but to fail or remain silent — a setup to obscure the real perpetrators.
source_quote: You're only being employed so you're likely to bungle the case...

subject: Who is the real Fheminor Scrivenbark?
fact: The absence of Fheminor Scrivenbark’s name from the team’s notes, despite their clear investigative alignment, raises a thread: is this person real, erased, or an impersonator themselves?
source_quote: It isn't… for some reason, there's no name on that entry.

subject: Who is the real killer?
fact: The true murderer is unknown; two suspects have emerged: one who knew the locket’s location and stole it, and another who rifled the safe; Kalan suspects a Great Reader, but Zalthir and Grygum have evidence that the safe-rifling may have been a decoy; the removal of the heart and use of Feywild poison suggest a ritualistic or magically sophisticated killer.
source_quote: Two hands had searched that apartment — one that knew exactly where to look, one that didn't.

subject: Why is the investigation time-limited?
fact: The team is told they must choose only a few threads before the situation moves on — but no reason is given; this urgency contradicts scholarly norms and suggests external forces are accelerating events.
source_quote: Apparently things keep happening while you're standing around thinking. Grygum put it plainest: 'There'll be more murders.'

subject: Zalthir’s missed lesson
fact: The thread of Zalthir’s ignorance regarding silent communication remains unaddressed. Glabbagool mastered the lesson Zalthir slept through — a failure that now defines their bond. The implication is that Zalthir’s growth as a shadow monk is incomplete, and his new powers are built on a foundation he never learned — a vulnerability disguised as strength.
source_quote: That, apparently, had been the day I was sleeping.
